sections.h2: What does the Douglas County Clerk of Superior Court record?
sections.html:
The clerk's Real Estate Division receives, indexes, scans and forwards every deed, lien, plat and UCC filing for Douglas County property. It also collects and disburses the fees that come with them, including the real estate transfer tax and intangible taxes. Each deed book holds about 1,050 pages, so a busy year fills several books.

The same office handles other records that affect a house sale. Federal, state and county tax liens and writs of fieri facias reach the clerk through the issuing agency. Real estate, UCC and civil protective order documents are scanned and sent to the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority, which also posts UCC filings online. Veterans' DD214 discharge papers are recorded for free and are no longer public record.

For land records or case files, the county directs callers to the Clerk of Superior Court at 770-920-7441. Wills and estate matters go to Probate Court at 770-920-7249.

sections.h2: Who can record a deed in Douglas County, and how?
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2025, anyone who is not on the state's professional list must file real estate documents electronically through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority. The change came from House Bill 1292 and covers every document recorded in the county's deed and lien records. A homeowner can no longer walk a deed to the counter and record it.

The county defines a self-filer as anyone outside these groups, so people in them keep their existing access:

  • Credit unions, mortgage lenders and mortgage servicers.
  • Georgia attorneys and Georgia surveyors.
  • Title insurance companies.
  • Georgia real estate brokers and salespersons.
  • Any public official.

Self-filers register at efile.gsccca.org and may only file through that site. The cooperative authority's help line is 1-800-304-5174, and its help address is help@gsccca.org. In practice the closing attorney or title company records the seller's deed, which is the simplest path for a house sale.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies when a Douglas County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Georgia charges real estate transfer tax before a deed can be recorded, and the clerk attaches a certification once it is paid. The Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000, and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100. It rests on the sale price.

The person who executes the deed, or the person who benefits from it, owes the tax. The department states that the seller is liable, though sales contracts often assign the cost to the buyer, so read that clause. The tax is filed with the PT-61 Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration, which the cooperative authority lets filers complete online.

Questions about whether a deed is taxable or exempt go to the Clerk of Superior Court. The Revenue Department's 2026 legislative update adds one change for transfer-on-death deeds under HB 413. A PT-61 is not needed when the deed is recorded, only when the beneficiary later records an acceptance affidavit.

sections.h2: How busy is the Douglas County real estate division?
sections.html:
The clerk's office reports 30,047 recorded instruments for 2024, up 2,296 from 2023. Real estate documents and liens make up nearly all of that volume, with a small number of plats and financing statements.

The county itself is large and growing. The Census Bureau estimates 154,293 residents for July 1, 2025 in 59,028 housing units, with a 66.9 percent owner-occupancy rate and a median owner-occupied home value of $296,900.

sections.h2: What fees should you expect at the Douglas County clerk's office?
sections.html:
The clerk publishes a fee sheet on the county website, and the version dated August 22, 2024 lists charges for deeds, liens, UCC filings, plats, copies and civil filings. It groups the real estate items by type. Deeds, including warranty, quitclaim, foreclosure, estate and security deeds, modifications, cancellations, affidavits and powers of attorney, sit together on the sheet. Lien items such as lis pendens, hospital liens, tax liens and assignments sit on a separate line.

Fee schedules change, so ask the clerk's office for the current figure before you budget. Add the transfer tax, which is calculated from the sale price and is separate from the recording fee. Your closing attorney or title company will list all of it on the settlement statement.

  • Recording fee: set by the clerk's published fee sheet.
  • Transfer tax: set by state law and based on the sale price.
  • E-filing: handled through the cooperative authority for self-filers.

sections.h2: What if you want to split a parcel or sell a Douglas County house?
sections.html:
A parcel split starts at Planning and Zoning, not at the clerk. A survey of the proposed change goes to the Zoning Administrator for approval under Article 5, Section 502 of the Douglas County Unified Development Code. After the stamped survey is recorded, the parties sign appropriately titled deeds and record them with the Clerk of Superior Court, through an attorney or the e-file system.

For an ordinary sale, the order is short. The seller signs a deed at closing, transfer tax is paid, and the clerk records the deed and certifies the tax. A buyer's lender then records the security deed. If an old lien, lis pendens or unpaid tax sits on the title, the closing agent will see it in the clerk's real estate index and require payoff first.

Sellers who inherited a house in Douglas County, owe back taxes or have tenants often prefer an as-is sale. The paperwork at the clerk is the same, and the cash buyer's closing attorney handles the e-filing so you do not need to register as a self-filer.

faqs.q: Can I record my own deed in Douglas County?
faqs.a: Only through the state e-file system. Since January 1, 2025, self-filers must file real estate documents electronically through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority, and the clerk's counter does not accept them. Attorneys, lenders, title companies, surveyors, brokers and public officials are outside that definition.

faqs.q: How much is the Georgia transfer tax on a Douglas County sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 of the sale price, with fractions rounded as the statute describes. The seller is liable by law, but contracts often shift it to the buyer.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Douglas County land records?
faqs.a: Call the Clerk of Superior Court at 770-920-7441 for land records and case files. Probate Court at 770-920-7249 handles wills and estates.

faqs.q: Is a PT-61 form required for a transfer-on-death deed in Douglas County?
faqs.a: No, not when the transfer-on-death deed is recorded. Under HB 413 as summarized by the Georgia Department of Revenue, the PT-61 is needed only when the beneficiary records an acceptance affidavit.

faqs.q: Does the Douglas County clerk record military discharge papers for free?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk records DD214 discharge records at no charge to the veteran, and they are no longer public record.
